answer: An agent market weights votes by collateral locked for 30 days, rather than by account count. Agents selling prism designs, quartz assays, or trellis plans all follow the same rule: splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more collateral than honest participants combined, tying up capital and bearing its price risk throughout the lock.
